decisions.reason: ACE3 is a core extension of the firm's airfield lighting control business, which supplies an installed base needing upgrades, so the COVID-era shortfall in airport spending is no reason to cut a product central to its established strength.

The air situation display fits the integrated tower and surveillance portfolio. Its evidence is thin and airport budgets were squeezed in 2020–2021, but it costs little to keep within the existing tower offer and supports the integration strategy.

Training programs build on existing know-how at low cost and support service revenue and customer retention, which matter more when new-system sales stall, so problemistic search would favour keeping them.
The airfield ground lighting course ties directly to the core lighting installed base and needs few resources, so it gives the firm no reason to drop it despite thin website evidence.

Collaboration software embodies the firm's stated direction toward data-driven, collaborative airport operations, and software is cheap to carry, so management would likely persist despite the aviation downturn.

The MLAT system is a flagship tied to the integrated-operations strategy. The pandemic shortfall and tight slack make this hardware-intensive surveillance line the most likely target of a portfolio review, but commitment to the flagship favours keeping it.
